requirement:
When the backend and model support prompt caching, every provider request MUST
place one cache checkpoint after the system prompt of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and another at the end of its last
message, so each request reuses the tool definitions and system prompt that
earlier assessments of its kind sent, and the conversation its own earlier
requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT change the content of a request.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation has code that carries it out and a test that checks it.

**Obligation: place cache checkpoints only when the backend and model support prompt caching.**
- `RigProvider::connect` (src/authoring/providers.rs:104-136) sets `caches` from the backend and model. For Bedrock it calls `bedrock_caches(&config.model)`, which is true only for the Claude and Nova families, the same families rig-bedrock accepts checkpoints for. For Ollama it is `false`, since Ollama has no prompt-cache checkpoints.
- `complete` (lines 180-200) calls `place_cache_checkpoints` only when `self.caches` is set, and it does so on every provider request.
- Tests:
  - `cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models` (providers.rs unit test) asserts `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude and Nova model ids and false for Llama and an unknown model.
  - `claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage` (tests/authoring_cli.rs:1797) asserts that a Claude run carries checkpoints and that `fixture-uncached-model` gets none.

**Obligation: put one checkpoint after the system prompt and another at the end of the last message, on every request.**
- `place_cache_checkpoints` sets `request.options.cache = Some(CacheRetention::Short)`.
- The vendored rig-bedrock `request::base` (vendor/rig-bedrock/src/request.rs:89-93) pushes a `cachePoint` block after the system blocks.
- The same function (lines 135-143) pushes a `cachePoint` block onto the content of the last message. This is a patch that places the checkpoint after reasoning turns too.
- The integration test checks both requests of the run. Each has `system.len() == 2` with `system[1]` equal to the checkpoint. The last message's last content block is the checkpoint, and exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences appear in each body. The second request follows a reasoning turn and still ends in a checkpoint.
- The unit test also checks that the cache option is set after a reasoning turn.

**Obligation: the system prompt of `prompt_parts` is the part that gets the checkpoint.**
- The integration test checks that `system[0]` text starts with `# Task`. That test also carries a `{test}` reference to `prompt_parts`. I treated `prompt_parts` as cited context and did not reassess it.
- Because the checkpoint follows the system prompt and the last message, each request reuses its earlier prefix.

**Obligation (MUST NOT): checkpoints do not change the content of a request.**
- The unit test compares the serialized request before and after placement. Only `options.cache` differs.
- The integration test runs the same conversation against a non-caching model and asserts `without_cache_points(cached) == plain` for each request.

**Unspecified behavior and reachability:** I found none. The `bedrock_caches` and `place_cache_checkpoints` helpers and the vendored encoder are all reached from the two `{impl}` items, `connect` and `complete`.

**Residual risk, not a gap:** `bedrock_caches` treats every Claude-family model as supporting caching, which is a judgment about "model support" that the text does not define more precisely.

Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
requirement, example, citation review, site review, and a verifier of each of
those. A system prompt MUST be the same for every assessment of its kind, so
every placeholder whose value depends on the subject MUST be in the subject
